name: Housesteads Roman Fort
text: Housesteads Roman Fort was an auxiliary fort on Hadrian's Wall, at Housesteads, Northumberland, England. It is dramatically positioned on the end of the 1-mile (1.6 km)-long crag of the Whin Sill over which the Wall runs, overlooking sparsely populated hills. It was called the "grandest station" on the Wall and is one of the best-preserved and extensively displayed forts.

depictions.name: Housesteads
depictions.text: Housesteads Roman Fort The Housesteads was the name given to a former Roman auxiliary fort on Hadrian's Wall in Northumberland, England. Like numerous other garrisons, it was during the Roman exodus from Britannia during the 5th century. By the 9th century, the abandoned fort was largely covered in snow and notably housed the prized and personal battleaxe of the shieldmaiden Lagertha, the wife of Ragnar Lothbrok.
